subject: Multi-region residency: EU/APAC private deployment topology review
messages:
From: Lukas Vogel <lukas@eu-consulting.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Aiko Yamamoto <aiko@apac-ops.co.jp>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the quick overview on Wednesday. NordicPay is running a pilot for transaction enrichment that must keep EU customer data at-rest and in-transit within EU boundaries for primary storage, but they also want an APAC standby region for DR and occasional read-only workloads for APAC customers. They asked for a short architecture proposal from Redwood that covers:

- VPC topology options (regional control planes vs single control plane)
- Cross-border replication rules and allowed traffic flows
- Key management (separate KMS per region?)
- How failover would work without violating residency during normal ops
- Operational runbook for DR tests (what we can promise)

I attached the compliance questionnaire they gave us and a rough network sketch. Can your team propose a topology and call out any known blockers for the months-long pilot (regulatory or technical)?

Appreciate it — want to keep the timeline tight (pilot kickoff target: Oct 15).

-Lukas

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Lukas Vogel <lukas@eu-consulting.io>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 02:45:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Hannah / all — quick technical take after sketching two options:

1) Dual-region isolated control planes (recommended for pilot)
   - Deploy two independent private control planes: one in an EU VPC (primary) and one in APAC VPC (standby).
   - Data-at-rest: EU primary holds canonical PII and transaction logs; backups replicated to APAC are encrypted and tagged as "DR-only"; access controls block restoration without manual approval (two-person approval).
   - KMS: Use region-specific KMS keys (EU KMS for EU data, APAC KMS for APAC resources). Cross-region key usage is disallowed by policy.
   - Failover: DNS-based traffic shift + load balancer re-pointing to APAC cluster. During failover, any request that requires PII restoration will be served only after documented manual approval — so failover is partial (compute can run, but PII restore requires justification).

2) Single control plane with regional data zoning (lower ops overhead, higher risk)
   - Control plane sits in EU but can orchestrate workloads in APAC. Requires strong network ACLs and strict egress filtering. Risk: control plane operator access could create data export vectors; legal team may push back.

Notes / blockers:
- Certification: APAC VPC must meet local certification if NordicPay plans to process non-EU APAC PII.
- Network: We recommend no automatic bi-directional replication of PII — only encrypted, one-way snapshot exports to APAC designated as "DR".
- Latency: For read-only APAC workloads, replicate pseudonymized/aggregated datasets rather than full PII sets when possible.

I'll attach a quick diagram and a short checklist. If we go dual-control-plane, we'll need an extra Dedicated capacity pool in APAC and an ops runbook for manual restore steps.

-Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260919-topology-proposal.png (PNG, 512KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Lukas Vogel <lukas@eu-consulting.io>, Aiko Yamamoto <aiko@apac-ops.co.jp>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Adding compliance/crypto perspective:

- KMS/HSM: Strong preference for KMS-per-region and HSM-backed key material for EU primary keys. We should include support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) stored in their EU KMS or HSM when they require it.
- Audit logs: Keep immutable audit logs in EU for at least 1 year (per their questionnaire). We can stream copies of logs to APAC for operational visibility, but those copies must be redacted or pseudonymized unless explicit approval is given.
- Failover policy: Define two tiers — (A) automatic compute-only failover (no PII restored) with <15m detection-to-standby time, (B) manual PII restore with multi-approver workflow and documented justification (RTO depends on dataset size; estimate 4–8 hours for full restore for pilot).
- Data procession consent: Confirm whether NordicPay treats hashed tokens as PII in their jurisdictions — this changes replication rules.

Blockers:
- If NordicPay needs automatic full-state failover (PII included) to APAC, legal will likely require Data Processing Agreements and possibly local legal review for cross-border transfers.
- Network peering: some APAC clouds restrict cross-region peering; we should validate with their cloud provider.

I'll draft language for the runbook and the compliance page.

-Priyom
Lead Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Vogel <lukas@eu-consulting.io>, Aiko Yamamoto <aiko@apac-ops.co.jp>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Lukas / Aiko — thanks for the patience and great questions. Summary of what we propose for the pilot (attached PDF + diagram):

- Topology: Dual isolated control planes: EU primary (canonical PII + live traffic), APAC standby (DR & read-only. no automatic PII restoration).
- Keys & crypto: Region-specific KMS; EU keys never exportable. Support for BYOK in EU if NordicPay requests it. HSM-backed keys for production.
- Replication: One-way encrypted snapshot exports to APAC labelled DR-only. Pseudonymized datasets recommended for read-only workloads.
- Failover: Two-tier approach — compute-only automatic failover for short outages; manual, multi-approver PII restore for full-failover events. Estimated manual restore RTO for pilot: 4–8 hours (depends on dataset size).
- Controls & evidence: Immutable EU audit logs retained per questionnaire; redacted copies to APAC for ops visibility. We'll provide an initial runbook and a checklist for DR drills.

Next steps / action items:
1) Vivek: finalize architecture diagram and deployment checklist (ETA Mon 27 Sep).
2) Priyom: draft runbook language and legal-friendly wording for the two-tier failover (ETA Wed 29 Sep).
3) Monica: coordinate capacity request for APAC Dedicated pool estimate and cost ballpark (ETA Tue 28 Sep).
4) Hannah: sync with Lukas on Tue 21 Sep to present this summary to NordicPay legal (calendar invite sent).

If NordicPay needs a model where APAC can handle full automatic failover of PII, we will need to escalate to legal & their procurement for additional contractual safeguards and potential local certifications. For the pilot timeline (Oct 15 kickoff) the dual-control-plane with manual-PII-restore fits best and keeps regulatory exposure minimal.

Best —
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
